questions_and_answers.question: One identical unit is purchased on each of the following three dates and at the respective costs: June 1 at $10 June 2 at $15 July 4 at $20 The company sells two units during the period. Conclude which inventory items are sold first and which unit remains in ending inventory if the company is using the FIFO cost flow assumption.
questions_and_answers.answer: The June 1 at $10 and the June 2 at $15 are both sold; the July 4 unit remains in ending inventory.

text_blocks.snippet: Under the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) inventory costing method, the unit sold on April 25th is assumed to be the one purchased on April 22nd for $17. The ending inventory would consist of the remaining units from earlier purchases, totaling $52 ($10 + $12 + $14 + $16).

list.title: LIFO Principle:
list.snippet: The LIFO method assumes that the most recently acquired inventory items are the first ones to be sold.

list.title: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS):
list.snippet: In this case, the unit sold on April 25th is assumed to be the unit purchased on April 22nd for $17. This cost is then recorded as COGS.
